title: Design a chat / messaging system (WhatsApp / Messenger)
relevance: High — classic 45-min HLD round at FAANG + Indian product cos (Meta, WhatsApp/Meta infra, Uber, Flipkart, Atlassian, PhonePe, etc.); probes WebSockets, stateful gateways, offline delivery, fan-out, and presence.
company_notes: Campus/intern/new-grad: very common WhatsApp/chat prompt covering WS vs polling, online path, offline store, and simple group fan-out. Mid-senior (1–4+ YOE): Redis pub/sub vs sticky hash, per-device sync, heartbeat/ACK failures, media pipeline, connection and write-QPS estimation — Meta/WhatsApp, Uber, Flipkart, Atlassian. Among top HLD prompts with URL shortener, news feed, rate limiter; depth stops at tradeoffs, not E2EE or Erlang OTP.

phases.goal: Scope 1:1/small-group chat vs Slack/Discord, lock functional NFRs, and park out-of-scope work.

must_hit.point: In scope: 1:1 + small group text, online/offline delivery, sent/delivered/read receipts, presence/last-seen, media via separate upload; optional typing indicators.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Lists 1:1 and small groups, offline delivery, receipt ladder, presence, and media off the chat path; may mention typing as optional.

must_hit.point: Explicitly out of scope: voice/video calls, Stories/channels at Discord scale, full E2EE crypto design, spam/abuse ML.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Says voice/video, Discord-scale channels, crypto implementation, and spam ML are deferred.

must_hit.point: NFRs: p99 delivery latency ≪ 500 ms when online; no silent message loss; high availability of gateways; store offline messages for days–weeks (e.g. 30d TTL) unless product says otherwise.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Cites sub-500 ms online latency, no silent loss, gateway HA, and multi-day offline retention such as 30d TTL.

must_hit.point: Clarify product framing: history forever on server (Messenger-like) vs store-until-delivered / client-primary (classic WhatsApp); cap group size early (e.g. 100 / 256 / 1024).
must_hit.evidence_hint: Asks whether server keeps forever history or client-primary store-until-delivered, and proposes a small group size cap like 100, 256, or 1024.

probes: What product are we designing—WhatsApp/Messenger small groups or Slack/Discord large channels—and what is explicitly out of scope?

hints.1: Start by naming the product flavor before drawing boxes.
hints.2: Separate functional (1:1, groups, receipts, presence, media) from NFRs (latency, durability, offline TTL) and call out Discord-scale and E2EE crypto as out of scope.
hints.3: State: 1:1 + small groups, offline store for days–weeks (e.g. 30d), p99 ≪ 500 ms online, no silent loss; clarify Messenger forever-history vs WhatsApp store-until-delivered; cap groups at 100/256/1024.

phases.goal: Agree round-number DAU, concurrent sockets, message and fan-out QPS, gateway count, and storage/presence load.

must_hit.point: Example scale: 500M DAU, ~25% concurrent online → ~125M open sockets.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Uses 500M DAU and ~25% concurrent to land ~125M open sockets.

must_hit.point: ~40 msgs/user/day → ~20B msgs/day ≈ ~230K msg/s average; peak 5–10×; with avg recipients ≈ 2–3 after 1:1 dominance, delivery QPS is a few× send QPS.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Walks ~40 msgs/user/day to ~20B/day ≈ ~230K msg/s, peak 5–10×, and delivery a few× send given ~2–3 recipients.

must_hit.point: Gateways at 100K–1M conns/box → hundreds–thousands of chat servers; WhatsApp Erlang lore includes millions/box (2M+ TCP connections/box).
must_hit.evidence_hint: Divides concurrent sockets by 100K–1M conns/box into hundreds–thousands of servers, optionally citing millions/box or 2M+ folklore.

must_hit.point: Storage: avg 100 B ciphertext + metadata; 20B/day → ~2 TB/day raw before replication/indexes; media dwarfs text → object store + CDN; presence heartbeats (e.g. every 30s) can dominate QPS—keep presence off the message DB write path.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Estimates ~2 TB/day from 100 B × 20B msgs, points media to object store/CDN, and warns 30s heartbeats must not hit the message DB.

probes: Walk me through concurrent connections, average/peak message QPS, and how many chat gateways you need.

hints.1: Pick DAU and percent online with the interviewer first.
hints.2: Derive open sockets from concurrent users, then msg/s from msgs/user/day, then gateway count from conns/box.
hints.3: Example: 500M DAU × ~25% → ~125M sockets; ~40 msgs/user/day → ~20B/day ≈ ~230K msg/s (peak 5–10×); 100K–1M conns/box → hundreds–thousands of servers; ~2 TB/day text at 100 B/msg; keep 30s presence heartbeats off the message DB.

phases.goal: Split HTTP control-plane from WebSocket chat commands and define ACK/sync on reconnect.

must_hit.point: REST/HTTP for signup/login, profile, create group, pre-signed media URL, and history pagination (if server history).
must_hit.evidence_hint: Lists HTTP endpoints for auth/profile/groups, pre-signed media URL, and optional history pagination.

must_hit.point: WebSocket commands (JSON/Protobuf): sendMessage {chatId, clientMsgId, ciphertext, attachmentRefs} → {serverMsgId, seq}; ack {messageId}; receipt {messageId, type}; presence / typing.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Names sendMessage with clientMsgId/ciphertext, ack, receipt types, and presence/typing over WS.

must_hit.point: Server → client: newMessage, receiptUpdate, chatUpdate; client must ACK so inbox can clear; auth token on WS handshake; reconnect with last seq / inbox sync.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Describes server pushes, client ACK clearing inbox, handshake token, and reconnect catch-up via last seq or inbox sync.

probes: What goes over HTTP vs WebSocket, and how does a client reconnect without losing messages?

hints.1: Think control-plane HTTP vs bidirectional chat transport.
hints.2: HTTP for auth/groups/media URLs/history; WS for send/ack/receipt/presence; reconnect carries last seq.
hints.3: REST: login, create group, pre-signed media URL, history; WS: sendMessage→{serverMsgId,seq}, ack, receipt, presence/typing; server pushes newMessage/receiptUpdate; token on handshake; reconnect syncs from last seq/inbox.

phases.goal: Model users/devices, chats/members, append-only messages, per-recipient inbox, and session/presence keys.

must_hit.point: User/Device: user_id with devices[device_id, push_token, last_seq]; Chat: chat_id, type (dm/group); ChatMember (chat_id, user_id) plus reverse index user_id → chat_id.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Shows device rows with push_token/last_seq and chat membership with a reverse user→chats index.

must_hit.point: Message: PK chat_id, SK seq or timestamp+id; fields sender_id, client_msg_id (unique), ciphertext, media_refs; wide-column/KV (Cassandra/Dynamo) fits append + time-range reads.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Uses chat_id + seq (or timestamp+id) with client_msg_id uniqueness and ciphertext/media_refs in an append-friendly store.

must_hit.point: Inbox (undelivered): PK user_id or device_id, SK message_id/time; TTL; delete on ACK; for small N, fan-out-on-write copies inbox rows per recipient.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Describes per-user or per-device inbox with TTL, delete-on-ACK, and per-recipient copies for small groups.

must_hit.point: Session: user_id → gateway_id (Redis); Presence: user_id → online|last_seen with TTL refreshed by heartbeat.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Puts session map and presence/last-seen with heartbeat TTL in Redis (or equivalent), separate from durable messages.

probes: How do you store messages, undelivered inbox rows, and which gateway a user is connected to?

hints.1: Separate durable chat history from undelivered inbox and ephemeral session/presence.
hints.2: Append messages by chat_id+seq; inbox keyed by user/device; session and presence in Redis with TTL.
hints.3: Message PK chat_id SK seq with client_msg_id; inbox PK user_id/device_id deleted on ACK with TTL; fan-out-on-write for small N; Redis user_id→gateway_id and presence TTL from heartbeats.

phases.goal: Draw clients, L4 LB, stateful WS gateways, durable message path, pub/sub routing, push, and media offload.

must_hit.point: Clients ↔ L4 LB ↔ chat gateway cluster (WS; local user→conn map); separate stateless API/Auth over HTTP.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Shows L4 LB into stateful WS gateways with local connection maps plus a separate HTTP auth/API service.

must_hit.point: Message service: validate → assign seq/id → durable write (messages + inboxes) then publish to pub/sub or Kafka; durability before best-effort realtime publish.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Persists message and per-recipient inbox first, then publishes; does not rely on pub/sub alone for durability.

must_hit.point: Routing backplane: Redis pub/sub sharded by user_id (or Kafka + workers that look up session and RPC/push to the right gateway); Session + Presence in Redis; Push service → APNs/FCM when offline.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Routes via sharded Redis pub/sub or Kafka+session lookup to the owning gateway; offline path uses APNs/FCM.

must_hit.point: Media: client → object storage via pre-signed URL; CDN for download; chat carries URL/hash, not blobs over WS. Happy path online 1:1: A→gateway → persist → pub/sub to B’s channel → B’s gateway → WS push → B ACK → clear inbox → delivery receipt to A.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Offloads media to pre-signed object storage/CDN and narrates persist→pub/sub→WS→ACK→receipt for online 1:1.

probes: Walk the online 1:1 path end-to-end when sender and receiver are on different gateways.

hints.1: Sender and receiver rarely share a host—something must route across gateways.
hints.2: Persist first, then pub/sub or Kafka to the receiver’s gateway via session registry; push if offline.
hints.3: A→gateway→message service durable write (messages+inbox)→Redis pub/sub (user-sharded)→B’s gateway→WS→ACK clears inbox→delivery receipt; offline uses APNs/FCM; media via pre-signed object storage.

phases.goal: Defend cross-gateway scale-out, group fan-out model, multi-device sync, flaky WS, ordering, and E2EE depth limits.

must_hit.point: Scale beyond one gateway: prefer sharded Redis pub/sub by user_id (durable inbox first) over Kafka topic-per-user; consistent-hash sticky users works but is painful on rebalance; naive LB without routing breaks delivery.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Rejects topic-per-user Kafka, favors user-sharded Redis pub/sub after durable inbox, and notes sticky hash rebalance pain.

must_hit.point: Group fan-out-on-write vs fan-out-on-read: write-amplification OK for ≤100–1K members; large channels store one log and let clients pull/cursor—different design from WhatsApp small groups.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Uses fan-out-on-write for ≤100–1K; switches to fan-out-on-read/log+cursor for Discord-scale channels.

must_hit.point: Multi-device: inbox/cursor per device; pub/sub still per user; all devices get copies; cap linked device count. WS death: app-level ping/pong; ACK timeout → close → reconnect → inbox catch-up; exponential backoff + jitter (thundering herd).
must_hit.evidence_hint: Per-device inbox/cursor, cap devices; ping/pong, ACK-driven reconnect with backoff+jitter, then inbox catch-up.

must_hit.point: Ordering & retries: per-conversation (or per-sender-in-chat) sequence—not global total order; client_msg_id dedupe; at-least-once + idempotent apply; exactly-once end-to-end is not the interview default. E2EE: mention Signal Protocol—server stores ciphertext + metadata; defer crypto.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Argues per-chat seq + client_msg_id idempotency and at-least-once; mentions Signal/ciphertext only, no Double Ratchet deep dive.

probes: How do you deliver when users are on different gateways, and when would you switch from fan-out-on-write to fan-out-on-read?

hints.1: Cross-gateway routing and group size drive most of the hard tradeoffs.
hints.2: Durable inbox + user-sharded pub/sub; fan-out-on-write only while groups stay small; per-device sync.
hints.3: Sharded Redis pub/sub by user_id after inbox write; fan-out-on-write for ≤100–1K, fan-out-on-read for large channels; per-device inbox; ping/pong + backoff reconnect; per-chat seq + client_msg_id; mention Signal, don’t implement.

phases.goal: Name connection, hot-key, write-path, presence, push, regional, and gateway-failure limits and mitigations.

must_hit.point: Connection count / FD limits on gateways → more boxes, efficient runtime (evented / Erlang-style), tune kernel socket limits; modern boxes hold 10⁴–10⁶ connections (WhatsApp lore: millions/box).
must_hit.evidence_hint: Cites FD/connection limits, horizontal scale, evented/Erlang-style runtimes, and 10⁴–10⁶ or millions/box lore.

must_hit.point: Hot users / large groups → adaptive pub/sub key (user vs chat), rate limits, degrade receipts/typing first; inbox/message DB write QPS → partition by user_id/chat_id, TTL compaction, don’t store media in DB.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Adaptive pub/sub keys, rate limits, degrade receipts/typing; partition writes; TTL; media out of DB.

must_hit.point: Presence heartbeat storm → separate store, coarser TTL, fan-out presence only to open chats/friends subset; push provider quotas → batch, quiet hours, collapse notifications.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Keeps presence off the message write path with separate store/coarser TTL/scoped fan-out; batches/collapses pushes.

must_hit.point: Regional latency → regional gateway pools + local session; cross-region for roaming. Failure: gateway death → clients reconnect elsewhere, re-subscribe pub/sub, drain inbox; no single gateway is source of truth for history.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Regional gateway/session pools; on gateway death, reconnect, re-subscribe, drain inbox—history is not on the gateway.

probes: What breaks first under load—connections, presence heartbeats, or inbox writes—and how do you scale each?

hints.1: List connection FDs, write QPS, and presence storms separately.
hints.2: Scale gateways horizontally; partition inbox/message writes; isolate presence; regionalize.
hints.3: More evented gateways for 10⁴–10⁶ conns/box; partition by user_id/chat_id; presence in separate store with coarser TTL; adaptive pub/sub for hot groups; regional pools; gateway death → reconnect + inbox drain, not history on the box.

tradeoffs.topic: Sharded Redis pub/sub by user_id vs Kafka topic-per-user vs sticky consistent-hash
tradeoffs.strong_answer: Durable inbox first, then sharded Redis pub/sub keyed by user_id for cross-gateway delivery. Kafka topic-per-user will not scale operationally at WhatsApp scale. Consistent-hash sticky users can work but rebalance is painful; naive LB without routing breaks delivery when sender and receiver are on different hosts.

For WhatsApp-style small groups, fan-out-on-write (copy inbox rows per recipient) is fine while write-amplification stays OK for ≤100–1K members. Large Discord-style channels should store one log and let clients pull/cursor (fan-out-on-read)—do not mix the two after the interviewer scoped small groups.

tradeoffs.topic: Per-device inbox vs shared user inbox
tradeoffs.strong_answer: Inbox/cursor per device; pub/sub can still be per user so all devices get copies; cap linked devices. Clearing a shared inbox when only one device ACKed drops messages for other devices.

Mention Signal Protocol: server stores ciphertext + metadata; server-side search/moderation and multi-device key management get hard. In a 45-min HLD, mention E2EE and defer crypto rather than deriving Double Ratchet.
HTTP for auth/profile/media URLs; WebSocket (or custom TCP) for bidirectional chat. Polling wastes battery; SSE is server→client only, so it is a poor fit for chat send path.

gotchas.trap: Drawing WebSockets then forgetting cross-server routing when users land on different gateways.
gotchas.correction: Add a session registry (user_id → gateway_id) and/or sharded pub/sub so the receiver’s gateway gets the message.

gotchas.trap: Using a Kafka topic-per-user for inbox/routing.
gotchas.correction: That is operationally impossible at WhatsApp scale; use durable inbox plus user-sharded Redis pub/sub (or Kafka with session lookup workers), not one topic per user.

gotchas.trap: Claiming exactly-once delivery without client idempotency / ACK.
gotchas.correction: Default is at-least-once to devices plus client ACK and idempotent message_id (client UUID); exactly-once end-to-end is not the interview default.

gotchas.trap: Putting images on the WS path or as DB BLOBs.
gotchas.correction: Pre-signed upload to object storage; chat message carries a URL/hash only.

gotchas.trap: Requiring global message ordering across all chats.
gotchas.correction: Order per-conversation (or per-sender-in-chat) with a sequence/partition key—not a global total order.

gotchas.trap: Treating presence as strongly consistent or writing every heartbeat to Cassandra.
gotchas.correction: Presence is eventual/lossy via heartbeats + Redis TTL/last-seen; keep it off the message DB write path.

gotchas.trap: Designing Discord-sized channels with WhatsApp fan-out-on-write (or vice versa) after small groups were scoped.
gotchas.correction: Cap group size early; use fan-out-on-write for small N and a different fan-out-on-read design for large channels.

gotchas.trap: Ignoring multi-device or clearing a shared inbox when only one device ACKed.
gotchas.correction: Per-device inbox or sync cursor; do not clear undelivered state for all devices on a single device ACK.

gotchas.trap: Reconnect thundering herd with synchronized retries after a regional outage.
gotchas.correction: Exponential backoff + jitter on reconnect; app-level ping/pong and inbox catch-up after ACK timeout.

gotchas.trap: Spending half the interview on Signal Protocol math.
gotchas.correction: Mention E2EE/ciphertext-at-rest on server; spend the round on delivery, storage, fan-out, and failure modes.
